extras.quota_verbatim: No storage. Free, no account, no card. Public relays are rate-limited per connection but the rate limits are deliberately unpublished. The paid Shared tier is the only one with published figures: 100 GB relayed egress/month then $0.09/GB, 5 MB/s, 10,000 concurrent connections.
extras.limits_verbatim: Not a storage provider. Only relayed bytes hit the operator, hence the per-connection rate limit rather than a byte quota.
extras.egress_verbatim: Free public relays, rate-limited. Self-hosting a relay is free and unlimited (open licence) — the cost moves to your own bandwidth.
extras.chaining_verbatim: This is SIGNALLING, not relaying, in the normal case: 'roughly 9 out of 10 connections go direct; the relay is only a fallback'. The relay carries bytes only when hole punching fails, which is what makes the free tier viable at all.
extras.tooling_verbatim: `iroh` crate; relay is a library, not a service with an upload endpoint
extras.interface_verbatim: QUIC over TLS 1.3; Rust crate `iroh`, bindings for other languages
extras.agent_focus: Systematic sweep of self-hosted academic repository software (Dataverse, DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, Fedora/Islandora) scored on the four client questions: institutional-email requirement, per-file cap, per-collection/dataset cap, and whether the install enforces a quota object at all. Primary method was machine probing, not page reading: /api/info/version and /api/dataverses/:root/storage/quota?showInherited=true against the full official Dataverse installation registry (150 hostnames), the native-signup form probe /dataverseuser.xhtml?editMode=CREATE against all 83 no-quota hosts, and the platform source defaults read out of the upstream config files for DSpace, InvenioRDM, EPrints, libp2p and iroh. Secondary coverage of the relay/P2P half of the slot.
